public_rationale: Part of the claim holds. Goldman Sachs counts $108 billion of hyperscaler debt in 2025 and $194 billion in 2026 by early August, plus nearly $500 billion of AI-related debt this year. So 'hundreds of billions of dollars of debt' is borne out. NVIDIA's filing also confirms its revenue is concentrated among a few customers. But the sentence's central charge is that these few buyers are mostly not using the GPUs. The evidence is only anecdotal: reports of Amazon staging racks at sites without power. Nothing representative shows most of their GPUs idle, or shows the opposite. The price and stock-market parts are rhetorical and were not measured. Because the main charge cannot be checked either way, the claim as a whole is unresolved.
limitations: Bank debt tallies use different definitions.
Usage evidence comes from secondary reports about one company.
The rhetorical parts ('every imaginable', 'most of our stock market') resist measurement.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Hundreds of billions of dollars of debt has been issued, the price of every imaginable consumer electronic has been inflated, and most of the stock market and parts of the economy have become dependent on GPU sales, most of which go to a handful of companies that are, for the most part, not using them.

statement.excerpt: Hundreds of billions of dollars of debt has been issued, the price of every imaginable consumer electronic has been inflated, and both most of our stock market and parts of our economy have become dependent on the sales of GPUs, most of which are going to a handful of companies that are, for the most part, not fucking using them.

from_speaker: Hundreds of billions of dollars of debt has been issued
the price of every imaginable consumer electronic has been inflated
most of our stock market and parts of our economy have become dependent on the sales of GPUs
most of which are going to a handful of companies
that are, for the most part, not fucking using them
our_interpretation: This is a compound claim. The plain reading is that each part must hold. The central factual charge, and the one the sentence builds to, is that most GPU sales go to a few companies that mostly are not using them.
'Hundreds of billions of dollars of debt' is read as cumulative AI-related debt issuance in the boom up to the post date. The target period runs from 2025-01 to the post date, 2026-09-22.
'Every imaginable consumer electronic' and 'most of our stock market' are rhetorical. They are read loosely as broad consumer electronics price rises and heavy market dependence on GPU sales.
'For the most part, not using them' is read as most GPUs bought by these few companies being uninstalled or idle at the time of the post.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that AI-related debt issuance reached hundreds of billions of dollars by September 2026, that consumer electronics prices rose broadly, that GPU sales are concentrated in a few buyers, and representative evidence that most GPUs those buyers bought were not in use.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that AI debt issuance was well below $200 billion, or representative evidence that most GPUs sold to the large buyers were installed and running around September 2026.

evidence.excerpt: These companies, the group of hyperscalers, issued $108 billion of debt globally in 2025. Fast-forward to 2026. So far this year, they've issued $194 billion.
evidence.locator: transcript, Amanda Lynam's answer on why hyperscalers use bond markets
evidence.explanation: Hyperscalers alone issued about $302 billion of debt from 2025 to early August 2026. That supports the 'hundreds of billions of dollars of debt' part.

evidence.excerpt: By our estimates, we track nearly $500 billion of AI-related debt issuance
evidence.locator: transcript, Amanda Lynam on the broader AI ecosystem
evidence.explanation: Broader AI-related debt issuance of nearly $500 billion in 2026 to date also supports the debt part.

evidence.excerpt: Our revenue is concentrated among a limited number of direct and indirect customers
evidence.locator: Note on segment information, customer concentration paragraph
evidence.explanation: NVIDIA confirms its revenue is concentrated in a few customers. That fits the 'handful of companies' part. It says nothing about whether those customers use the GPUs.

evidence.excerpt: Some of these racks are being staged in facilities with plenty of floor space but not enough power supply to activate them.
evidence.locator: section 'Racks arriving faster than the grid can keep up', paragraph 3
evidence.publisher: Crypto Briefing (citing ZeroHedge and Business Insider)
evidence.explanation: Shows that one big buyer had some racks idle for lack of power. That is far short of showing the large buyers are 'for the most part' not using their GPUs.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Disclosures or credible estimates from the largest GPU buyers of installed and running GPUs versus GPUs purchased, around September 2026.
